core_obligations: Set up the conormal sequence (proof lines 1015-1030): composing with the closed immersion of the blowup into the projective line over the base gives an exact sequence from the conormal sheaf to the pullback of the differentials of the projective line to the differentials of the blowup; since the restriction of those pullback differentials to the exceptional divisor is the module of differentials of the exceptional curve over the residue field, it suffices to show that the first arrow maps onto the kernel of the canonical restriction map.

Verify the surjectivity locally (proof lines 1030-1042): on an affine open of the blowup the morphism from the base corresponds to the quotient of a polynomial ring in one variable by the relation expressing the product of a generator of the maximal ideal with the variable as the other generator; the differential of that relation is the first generator times the differential of the variable, and the second generator times the differential of the variable is a multiple of it, so the conormal generator maps onto the kernel and the identification follows.
proof_roadmap: Use the conormal sequence of the closed immersion into the projective line.
Identify the restriction of the pullback differentials with the differentials of the exceptional curve.
Check the required surjectivity in the local model.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the differentials of the blowup of the maximal ideal of a regular local surface over the base are the pushforward of the differentials of the exceptional divisor over the residue field (statement lines 1011-1014). The proof (proof lines 1015-1042) uses the conormal sequence of the closed immersion into the projective line, identifies the restriction of the pullback differentials, and verifies the surjectivity in the explicit local model. H2: a complete short computation in two steps.
